# B2B Fintech Support

`customer_support.model.b2b.fintech` · vertical · parent `customer_support.model.b2b`

> Supporting businesses whose money moves through us — payments infrastructure, banking-as-a- service, lending and treasury platforms. Three structural facts change the work. The ticket is a regulated record. Whatever an agent writes may be read later by an auditor, a regulator or opposing counsel, and the reconstruction has to hold years after everyone who touched it has left. That makes the audit trail a deliverable of support rather than a by-product of it, and it makes "I fixed it quietly" a compliance failure even when the customer is delighted. The clock is frequently statutory rather than contractual. A regulated complaint and a reportable incident both carry externally-set deadlines that outrank whatever the support plan promised, and missing one is an enforcement matter, not a CSAT dip. Money movement is close to irreversible and agents cannot touch it. Support diagnoses and routes; a funds action requires dual control from a team that does not report into the queue. The naive retry — the reflex every software support agent has — can duplicate a payment, and the second payment is somebody's actual money. The error carried in from B2B SaaS is treating diagnosis data as freely shareable. Card data, account numbers and personal data cannot be pasted into a ticket or a Slack thread, so the normal "send me a screenshot" loop is unavailable and the reproduction discipline has to be built out of sanitised references instead.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | an engineer, operations analyst or compliance officer at the customer; the compliance requester is not asking a technical question and answering them technically fails |
| typical_resolution_hours | 16 |
| volume_shape | moderate and steady, with hard spikes at settlement cutoffs, month-end reconciliation and any payment-network incident |
| staffing_model | tiered, with a segregated funds-operations team support can route to but never act as, plus a named compliance liaison |
| coverage | extended hours aligned to settlement windows, on-call around clearing cycles and for any money-movement severity-1 |
| automation_level | low to moderate — deflection is capped by the fact that most questions are about one specific transaction that only we can see |
| notes | Deliberately no automation of the resolution itself. Reading a balance is deflectable; changing one is not, and every attempt to automate the second has ended as an incident.  |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.ticket`

Requires `created_at`, `first_response_at`, `assignee_ref`, `resolution_type`


> These four are the minimum reconstructible record — when it arrived, when we first answered, who held it, and what we actually did about it. They are mandatory here not because the queue needs them but because an audit does, and a field that is optional is a field that is empty on the one ticket someone eventually asks about.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.escalation`

Requires `origin`, `reason`, `receiving_owner_ref`


> Origin has to distinguish a customer asking for a manager from a regulated complaint being raised, because the second starts a statutory clock and the first does not. An escalation logged without that distinction is indistinguishable from an ordinary unhappy customer until the deadline has already passed.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.incident`

Requires `is_customer_visible`, `declared_at`, `affected_account_count`


> Reportability is assessed from these. Regulatory notification windows run from the point of detection rather than the point of resolution, so an incident whose declaration time is reconstructed afterwards from chat scrollback is already a finding.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.sla_target`

Requires `is_contractual`


> Here it separates two clocks that look the same on a board: the one we sold and the one a regulator imposes. When they conflict the statutory one wins, and an agent who does not know which they are looking at will prioritise the wrong ticket with total confidence.
